Who we are

Two homelands,
one table.

Club Bangla brings together students of Bengali heritage — from Bangladesh, West Bengal, and everywhere the diaspora has carried us — alongside anyone at Columbia curious enough to pull up a chair and share a plate of biryani. We're a home for the language, the festivals, and the small daily rituals of adda and cha that make a big city feel like home.

BangladeshWest BengalDiasporaAll are welcome
Two crests, side by side.

We drew our own marks: the King's Crown over Columbia's limestone columns, and the shapla — Bangladesh's national water lily — rising under a red sun. An Ivy League home for a Bengali heart.

&

Two emblems, one club — the King's Crown of Columbia and the shapla of Bengal.

What we celebrate

A year lived in Bangla.

From the first alpona of spring to the last cup of cha in December, our calendar keeps Bengali time.

Ekushey February একুশে

On International Mother Language Day we gather at our own Shaheed Minar to honour the martyrs of 1952 — the students who died so Bangla could be spoken freely. Candles, poetry, and "আমার ভাইয়ের রক্তে রাঙানো."

Pohela Boishakh

পহেলা বৈশাখ

The Bengali New Year — panta-ilish, red-and-white, alpona underfoot, and a Boishakhi mela that takes over the lawn.

Cha & Adda

চা ও আড্ডা

Our bread and butter: weekly hangouts over milk tea and endless conversation. No agenda, just good company.

Biryani Nights

খাওয়া-দাওয়া

Kacchi, fuchka, mishti — food is how we say hello. Potlucks and catered feasts that taste like someone's Nanu's kitchen.

Bijoy & Beyond

বিজয় দিবস

Victory Day, Independence Day, mentorship for first-years, and a spring formal that sends everyone off in style.

Our corner of New York

At home on Morningside Heights.

From the Low Steps to Butler at midnight, this campus is the backdrop to everything we build together — a Bengali table set beneath Ivy limestone.

We fly the Lion of Columbia and the flag of Bangladesh from the same table — দুই দেশ, এক পরিবার.

Get involved

Pull up a chair.

You don't need to speak a word of Bangla or trace your family to the Padma. If you're curious, hungry, or just looking for people — you already belong here. Drop your details and we'll add you to the list.
